newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Foreign investment in Argentina a record $14 bln.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Argentina a record $14 bln.

text.p: Foreign investment in Argentine stocks and bonds reached a record $14.1 billion in September, Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said on Monday.
The previous record was $13.3 billion in September 1993.

In a speech at the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange, Fernandez said the high level of foreign investment in equities and bonds was a reflection of "the confidence Argentina has generated abroad thanks to its (economic) stability."
He also reiterated previous estimates putting economic growth at 3.0 percent this year and 5.0 percent in 1997.
Fernandez was speaking at a ceremony launching Banco Hipotecario Nacional's first mortgage-backed peso bonds.

The mortgage bank, which is soon to be privatized, said it aims to place between 50-70 million pesos of this first series of bonds with local investors, mostly private pension funds, before the end of the month. The portfolio to be securitized is made up of 20,723 loans amounting to 212 million pesos.
